subject: EdgeFin benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.raines@edgefin.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: SLO targets + benchmark methodology (post-call)

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Tom - great to hear more about EdgeFin's real-time summarization use case. Quick recap + next steps so we're aligned: 

- Your top-level SLOs: p95 latency <= 200ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), streaming support for partial results, and sustained throughput target ~300 req/s for peak windows.
- Concurrency expectation: ~40 simultaneous live sessions; average session has ~2 requests/sec but bursts up to 6.
- Quality constraints: you need no regression versus your on-prem transformer baseline for the top-10 prompt families.

Action items we agreed on: 
1) You to share a representative prompt set + any label/eval expectations (we can accept CSV or a Drive folder).
2) We run Redwood's benchmark harness against your prompts and return: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput curves, tokens/sec, memory footprint, and streaming time-to-first-byte.
3) Agree measurement definitions (we included our initial methodology draft attached).

Please confirm the SLO numbers above and attach the prompt set when convenient. If the prompt set contains PII or sensitive examples, drop it in the Drive link with your access policy and we'll sign the access request.

Attaching: redwood_benchmark_methodology_v1.pdf (draft)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

---
From: Tom Raines <tom.raines@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-03-06T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO targets + benchmark methodology (post-call)

Thanks Marissa - that summary matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed SLOs: p95 <= 200ms (short prompts <=256 tokens). For longer prompts (256-1024 tokens) we expect p95 <= 500ms as a soft target.
- Sustained throughput: 300 req/s is correct for peak sustained windows; concurrent active sessions ~40 as you noted.
- Streaming: required. Important metric for us is time-to-first-token and ability to push partial updates within 60ms of generation start.

I've uploaded an initial prompt set and metadata to the Drive folder (edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv). The CSV includes: prompt_id, category, avg_input_tokens, expected_output_tokens, and a quality_label column for our internal pass/fail. 

Also attaching a short note about our session affinity (we reuse per-session KV cache for up to 5 minutes). If that impacts your methodology, let us know.

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv

We'll be available for a short sync with engineering if you want to walk through the prompt families.

- Tom Raines
Director, Platform Engineering - EdgeFin
tom.raines@edgefin.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.raines@edgefin.com>, Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: SLO targets + benchmark methodology (post-call)

Appreciate the prompt set, Tom - digging in and a couple of engineering clarifications so our benchmark is apples-to-apples: 

1) Input length distribution: can you confirm the 10/50/90 token percentiles for each prompt category? The CSV had avg_input_tokens but we prefer explicit percentiles for sampling.
2) KV cache: you mentioned per-session reuse up to 5 minutes - does that mean session affinity is sticky to a single instance or can sessions be routed across hosts (we'll simulate both)?
3) Allowed fallbacks: if a model variant is slower we may need to fallback to a lower-quantized variant; do you want us to include fallbacks in the report or only measure the primary model?
4) Streaming semantics: for the time-to-first-token metric, confirm whether you need us to measure from request arrival or from first token produced by model (we typically report both).

We're planning to run the first pass next week using our reproducible harness (Docker image + runner). I've attached the test-harness-spec for visibility. Please point out anything missing.

Thanks - Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Raines <tom.raines@edgefin.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO targets + benchmark methodology (post-call)

Answers inline: 

1) Percentiles: we'll export the 10/50/90 percentiles per category and drop them in the Drive folder by EOD.
2) Session affinity: sessions are sticky at the load balancer layer for ~3 minutes; we do allow routing across hosts afterwards. Simulate sticky and non-sticky routing.
3) Fallbacks: please measure the primary model only for the initial run; include auxiliary runs that show fallback behavior but keep them separate in the report.
4) Streaming TTF: measure both - request-arrival-to-first-byte and model-internal-first-token time.

I'll add the percentiles and a short note on traffic shape to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-edgefin-bench-prompts).

- Tom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Raines <tom.raines@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO targets + benchmark methodology (post-call)

Perfect - thanks Tom & Priya. Plan and next steps from Redwood: 

- We will: 
  * Pull the prompt set + percentiles from your Drive folder. 
  * Run a primary benchmark targeting your primary model variant (no fallbacks) and report: p50/p95/p99 latencies, sustained throughput curve up to 300 req/s, tokens/sec, memory, and streaming TTF metrics.
  * Run an auxiliary fallback pass and keep results separate.
  * Bundle the run artifacts (Docker image tag, runner config, raw logs, and scripts) so you can reproduce locally.

- Timeline: first-pass benchmark and draft results by 2027-03-19 EOD. We'll book a 30-min readout for the week of 3/22 to walk findings and next steps.
- Logistics: we'll need an S3/Drive link with the final prompt set + any PII redaction notes. If you prefer, we can run over a synthetic anonymized set - just let us know.

Attaching: redwood_benchmark_methodology_v2.pdf (updated per call) and benchmark-run-plan.xlsx (schedule + runner config).

If that timeline works I'll send a calendar invite for the readout and loop in our infra lead for any quota/whitelisting.

Thanks again - looking forward to running this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
